The 2027 Hyundai Elantra is a totally redesigned compact sedan that aims to offer premium style and features at an affordable price.

## What’s New for the 2027 Hyundai Elantra


The 2027 Hyundai Elantra is an all-new model that ushers in the eighth generation of this compact sedan. One of Hyundai’s longest-running cars, the Elantra gets dramatic new styling and the automaker’s latest infotainment tech, while continuing to offer a long list of features and sensible powertrain options. That includes a redesigned Elantra Hybrid, arriving as a 2028 model, **which we cover separately** .


## Design


Even compared with the previous-generation, which didn't exactly look plain, the 2027 Elantra makes quite a statement. Like the Tucson crossover (also redesigned for 2027), the Elantra’s styling incorporates boxy fender flares and sharp lines, but its complex surfaces are even more creative than the Tucson’s, giving this humble nameplate a truly futuristic look. Helping to sell that look is a wider and lower stance, accentuated by new “H-Edge” lighting elements that blend nicely with the exterior. The taillights even help optimize airflow, according to Hyundai, contributing to a fairly low drag coefficient of 0.26. A full list of trim levels and options was not available at the time of writing, but Hyundai confirmed that it will offer wheels up to 18 inches and some new paint colors, including Kodiak Blue (in pearl and matte finishes) and Graphene Green Pearl.


## Powertrain


While the design takes risks, the powertrain plays it safe. Non-hybrid models will be offered only with a naturally aspirated 2.0-liter four-cylinder engine, a continuously variable transmission (CVT), and front-wheel drive (FWD). This is the same setup used in most versions of the 2026 Elantra, and should be good for the same 147 horsepower. It should also match the 35 mpg combined EPA fuel-economy rating of the 2026 Elantra in at least some configurations. For now, Hyundai isn’t discussing plans for a new Elantra N-Line or Elantra N, but we wouldn’t be surprised if these sportier models return in the future.


## Interior


The cabin has some interesting design elements of its own, including a round center console and dashboard, the latter working well with the available ambient lighting. Ovoid housings for the door panels continue the theme, and give an often-overlooked area a distinctive appearance. The redesigned Elantra is 3.3 inches longer, 1.1 inches wider, and 0.3 inches taller than the outgoing model. It also has a wheelbase that’s 1.1 inches longer. All that translates to an additional 1.1 inches of rear-seat legroom and an extra 0.7 inches of headroom in both rows, according to Hyundai. The 13.9 cubic feet of trunk space is slightly less than in the outgoing Elantra, but still within segment norms. That stylish center console also affords generous small-item storage space for a compact car, including dual wireless device chargers.


## Technology


A 9.9-inch digital instrument cluster and a 12.9-inch touchscreen are shared with the redesigned 2027 Tucson, as is the underlying Pleos Connect infotainment system, which is intended to provide greater scope for new digital features such as an AI voice assistant (called Gleo) but retains wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto connectivity. Pleos Connect also enables a new layout that’s meant to minimize distraction. The instrument cluster is perched atop the dashboard so it’s always within the driver’s line of sight, and it only shows the most vital information. Everything else is located on the touchscreen, which itself is split so that functions the driver is more likely to use are on the left side, within easier reach. Hyundai has also included a few analog controls so drivers don’t have to rely solely on the touchscreen. The Elantra’s wireless device chargers operate at 15 watts, so drivers can stream music to the available Bang & Olufsen audio system without draining their phone's battery. Digital key tech will also be available.

## Safety


The 2027 Elantra will offer expected driver-assistance features such as forward-collision warning, automatic emergency braking, adaptive cruise control, blind-spot monitors, rear cross-traffic alert, lane-keep assist, high-beam assist, and a driver-attention monitor. Like other current Hyundai models, the 2027 Elantra will also be available with remote smart parking assist, parking sensors, a surround-view camera system, and blind-spot cameras. Safety ratings from the Insurance Institute for Highway Safety (IIHS) and National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) weren’t available at the time of writing. The outgoing Elantra was a 2026 IIHS Top Safety Pick and received a five-star overall safety rating from the NHTSA, setting a high bar for the new model.


## Pricing and Release Date


Pricing for the 2027 Hyundai Elantra was not available at the time of writing, but a slight increase from the 2026 model’s $24,120 base price (including a $1,295 destination charge) wouldn’t be surprising. Production for the United States starts in the first quarter of 2027, so we expect to see the redesigned Elantra in showrooms before the middle of the year.
